also: take the washing off the line

terms.comment: Our description: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no phrase for hanging out the washing and no word for a clothes line or a clothes peg (Morgan–Owens has vestīmenta lavāre, to do the laundry). Fūniculus, a cord (Cic.).

phrases.latin: Pluit! Vestīmenta dē fūniculō dētrahe et intrō fer.
phrases.english: It’s raining! Take the clothes off the line and bring them in.

phrases.latin: Jam sicca sunt vestīmenta; collige ea in corbem.
phrases.english: The washing’s dry now; gather it into the basket.

sources: Lewis & Short: funiculus · Lewis & Short: detraho · Lewis & Short: corbis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. laundry: do the laundry.
